core_obligations: Record that dimension at a point is the minimum of the Krull dimensions of the open neighbourhoods, so that each inequality may be proved one neighbourhood at a time (proof lines 5396-5399).

Prove that the dimension of V at v is at least the dimension of U at u: choose an open neighbourhood U' of u realising the dimension, push a chain of irreducible closed subschemes of U' forward, and check that consecutive images stay distinct because the fibres of f are discrete (proof lines 5402-5416).

Prove the reverse inequality: take an open neighbourhood U' of u, note that its image is an open neighbourhood of v, lift a chain of irreducible closed subschemes of that image by lifting its generic point, and apply going down to the induced flat local map of local rings to lift the chain of specializations into U' (proof lines 5419-5443).
proof_roadmap: Fix the meaning of dimension at a point (proof lines 5396-5399).
First inequality, by pushing a chain forward using discreteness of the fibres (proof lines 5402-5416).
Second inequality, by lifting a chain with going down for the flat local map of local rings (proof lines 5419-5443).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for an etale morphism of schemes f : U to V and points u in U, v = f(u), the dimension of U at u equals the dimension of V at v (statement lines 5389-5393). The proof first fixes what the notation means, namely the minimum of the Krull dimensions of the open neighbourhoods of the point, and then proves the two inequalities separately (proof lines 5396-5399). For the first, a chain of irreducible closed subschemes of an open neighbourhood of u is pushed forward along f; the images form a chain of specializations in V, and the crucial point that consecutive images are distinct uses that the fibres of an etale morphism over a field are discrete (proof lines 5402-5416). For the second, the image of an open neighbourhood is open, a chain in V is lifted by choosing a preimage of its generic point and applying going down to the flat local ring map on the local rings, which is what makes the lifted specializations land in the chosen neighbourhood (proof lines 5419-5443). The claim is H2: two genuinely different arguments are needed, the first resting on the discreteness of the fibres and the second on going down for a flat local map, and both are displayed in full; nothing here is a citation-only step and nothing beyond the standard dimension and flatness machinery is required.
